draft.ask: ASK: My small bowel is joined to my colon. Which oral rehydration solution, or recipe, has the right amount of sodium for me?

careTeamAnswers.summary: Reported by another user (no colon) from their own care team: their dietitian said many store-bought rehydration drinks have less sodium than what is used for short bowel, and gave them a recipe she approved.
Reported by another user (ileostomy) from their own care team: their doctor said the WHO formula was made for sudden diarrhea, and they needed more salt.
Reported by another user (no colon) from their own care team: their dietitian said a little lemon or sugar-free flavoring is usually fine, but to avoid flavorings made with sorbitol.

diagram.label: Salt and glucose together help the small bowel absorb water

sourcesChecked: Guidelines: Parrish & DiBaise 2017 (ORS sodium, colon in continuity, salt)
Care-team answers reported by other users
draft.verdict: For a small bowel joined to the colon, I found no concern about oral rehydration solution in nothing in the sources I checked. The guidelines name it as the preferred drink for short bowel syndrome, but how much sodium it has matters.

why.claim: A glucose-and-salt oral rehydration solution is the preferred drink for replacing fluid and salt losses in short bowel syndrome.
It works because glucose and sodium are absorbed together in the small bowel, and they pull water in with them.
For short bowel syndrome, solutions with about 90 to 120 mmol/L of sodium are usually recommended. That is more sodium than many store-bought rehydration drinks have.
The standard WHO formula has 75 mmol/L of sodium. It was made for sudden diarrhea, and its sodium is below the range usually cited for short bowel syndrome.
With the colon still connected, the colon also absorbs water and salt. So plain drinks like water are often handled better than they are by people with no colon.
8 of 12 people with a small bowel joined to the colon logged that oral rehydration solution helped. 2 said it was neutral and 2 said it hurt.

draft.ask: ASK: I have an ileostomy and my colon isn't connected. Is there a sweet treat without sorbitol or xylitol that won't raise my output?

careTeamAnswers.summary: Another user (with an end-jejunostomy) reported that their own dietitian said sugar-free candies often use sugar alcohols that can make things worse, not better.

sourcesChecked: Care-team answers reported by other users

swapToAskAbout.text: Banana is something to ask about if you want something sweet. Two people suggested it in place of sugar-free candy, 1 of them with an ileostomy, and 1 clinician endorsed it. Starchy foods like bananas are often reported to thicken output.

draft.verdict: Sugar-free candy made with sorbitol and xylitol could raise your ileostomy output, so it's worth asking your team before you have it.

why.claim: Sorbitol and xylitol are sugar alcohols. Your body doesn't absorb them well. They pull water into the gut and can raise stoma output or cause diarrhea. They are common in sugar-free products.
Regular candy isn't an easy fix either. Sweets with a lot of sugar also pull water into the bowel, and people with short bowel are usually told to limit them.
Of 13 people with an ileostomy who logged sugar-free candy, 9 said it made things worse, 4 said it made no difference, and none said it helped.
Another user reported what their own dietitian told them: sugar-free candies often use sugar alcohols that can make things worse, not better. That person has a different anatomy (end-jejunostomy).

careTeamAnswers.summary: Another user with an ileostomy reported that their own stoma nurse said sugar-free gum often has sorbitol or xylitol and is a common hidden cause of higher output.

sourcesChecked: Community tolerance logs for sugar-free gum

swapToAskAbout.text: Salted crackers are something to ask about instead. Two people posted this swap, one of them with an ileostomy. It passed a guideline check when posted, but no clinician has endorsed it.

draft.verdict: Sugar-free gum is flagged because it contains sorbitol, a sugar alcohol that can raise stoma output, so it's worth asking your care team before you use it.

why.claim: Sorbitol and other sugar alcohols are poorly absorbed. They pull water into the gut and can raise stoma output. Sugar-free products often contain them.
People with an ileostomy have a higher risk of dehydration and low salt, so anything that raises output matters more.
Of 14 people with an ileostomy who logged sugar-free gum, 7 said it hurt, 7 noticed no change, and none said it helped.

draft.verdict: Cookies are a sweet, sugary food, and short bowel guidelines say to generally limit concentrated sugars, so this is worth checking with your dietitian.

why.claim: Concentrated simple sugars, like sweets, pull water into the bowel. Guidelines say to generally limit them in short bowel syndrome.

Your colon is still connected. That means gut bacteria in the colon can win back some energy from starchy foods. So for bodies like yours, a diet richer in complex carbohydrates (starches) is usually preferred over sugary ones.
Some sugar-free cookies use sugar alcohols such as sorbitol or xylitol. Those can pull water into the gut and cause more diarrhea.
People with your anatomy who logged cookies: 1 said they helped, 9 noticed no change, and 4 said they made things worse.

draft.verdict: There's nothing in the sources I checked against banana for a small bowel joined to the colon, and guidelines list it among foods often reported to thicken output.

why.claim: Bananas are on a guideline list of starchy, low-fiber foods (with white rice, potatoes, pasta and plain crackers) that people often report thicken their output.
When the colon is still connected, bacteria in the colon can recover some energy from complex carbohydrates (starches). That's why a diet richer in them is usually favored for your group.

final.verdict: Adcirca is a plain immediate-release tablet, and I found nothing in the sources I checked that flags it for your anatomy, but with under 100 cm of small bowel, how well you absorb it is still worth checking.

why.claim: Adcirca is an immediate-release, film-coated tablet.
Most medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel. When that part is still there, many plain immediate-release medicines can still be absorbed.
How well medicines are absorbed depends more on the length and health of the small bowel that is left than on the type of stoma.
Food does not change how much of the medicine is absorbed. The label says it has not been measured how much of an oral dose reaches the body in total.
The product data I checked lists croscarmellose sodium, but the full inactive-ingredient section was missing, so I could not check all inactive ingredients.

evidence.G:aga-sbs#antimotility: Antimotility medicines (for example loperamide) are a mainstay to slow transit and reduce output; timing relative to meals is set by the care team.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#diet-simple-sugars: Concentrated simple sugars (sweets, syrups, sweetened drinks) draw water into the bowel and are generally limited in short bowel syndrome.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-release-forms: After extensive small-bowel resection, sustained-release and delayed-release (including enteric-coated) medicines are generally avoided because they depend on a long, normal transit to release the drug.
evidence.G:pd-2017#lactose: Lactose does not need to be removed for most people with short bowel syndrome; small portions of dairy, especially cheese and yogurt, are often tolerated.
evidence.G:pg139#crushing-immediate-release: For plain immediate-release tablets only, crushing or dissolving may improve absorption in some patients; this is a decision for the pharmacist. Crushing extended-release or enteric-coated products defeats their design and can be dangerous.
evidence.G:pg139#enteric-coating: Enteric-coated and delayed-release products are designed to pass the stomach before dissolving; with rapid transit, the coating may not dissolve in time, and some pass through intact.
evidence.G:pg139#liquid-forms: Liquid forms may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets in short bowel syndrome, but liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols that can increase output.
evidence.G:pg139#sugar-alcohols: Sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol and other sugar alcohols are poorly absorbed, draw water into the gut, and can raise stoma output or diarrhea; they are common inactive ingredients in liquid medicines and sugar-free products.
evidence.G:pg139#time-release: Time-release formulations depend on adequate small-bowel transit time to release their drug; with a shortened bowel or rapid transit, part of the dose may leave the body before it is released.
evidence.G:sood-2013#residual-length: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.
evidence.L:dosage_forms_and_strengths: immediate … orange, film-coated, almond-shaped tablets (not scored)
evidence.L:pharmacokinetics: Absolute bioavailability of tadalafil following oral dosing has not been determined. The rate and extent of absorption of tadalafil are not influenced by food; thus ADCIRCA may be taken with or without food.

draft.ask: ASK: I have a colostomy. Is my diltiazem the plain immediate-release tablet, or an extended-release kind that might not be absorbed as well?

diagram.label: Most medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel

sourcesChecked: Guidelines: AGA SBS update, Sood 2013, Remane 2025
draft.verdict: For plain immediate-release diltiazem tablets, I found nothing in the sources I checked that raises a concern for a colostomy with over 200 cm of small bowel.

why.claim: This label is for a plain tablet, not a slow-release one.
Diltiazem is well absorbed from the gut. Your liver breaks down a lot of it on the first pass, so about 40% reaches the blood. That's true for everyone, not just people with an ostomy.
Most medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel. Plain immediate-release medicines can usually still be absorbed when that part is there.
With a colostomy, most of the small bowel is usually intact, and medicines are often absorbed normally. This isn't a guarantee.
Plain fast-dissolving tablets are in the lowest-risk group for ostomy patients. Extended-release products are in the highest-risk group, and diltiazem also comes in extended-release forms.
The label says not to split these tablets.

draft.ask: ASK: I have an ileostomy and no colon in use. Will Coreg CR release and absorb fully for me, or would an immediate-release carvedilol work better?

diagram.label: Slow-release products can rely on the colon for part of their release

sourcesChecked: Guidelines: extended-release absorption with an ileostomy

swapToAskAbout.text: Ask whether a plain, quick-dissolving (immediate-release) form of carvedilol could work for you. Studies of people with an ostomy rated that kind of tablet as lower risk than extended-release. Only your prescriber can decide this.

draft.verdict: Coreg CR is an extended-release capsule, and this kind of product may not release all of its medicine in a body without a working colon, so it's worth asking your pharmacist about.

why.claim: Coreg CR is an extended-release capsule.
The label says the capsule and what's inside it should not be crushed, chewed, or split into smaller doses.
Even in a typical gut, the label says Coreg CR gives about 85% of the medicine that the immediate-release tablets give.
Slow-release products may release part of their medicine in the large bowel. Without a colon, they have less time and less gut surface to release it.
Time-release products need enough time in the small bowel. If food and medicine move through quickly, part of the dose may leave the body before it is released.
A study of people with an ostomy grouped extended-release products as 'critical', meaning the most likely to have trouble dissolving.
How well medicines are absorbed depends more on how much small bowel is left, and how healthy it is, than on the type of stoma. You have over 200 cm of small bowel, which may help.

draft.verdict: I found nothing in the sources I checked suggesting this cefdinir capsule is the wrong form for your body. It is a plain immediate-release capsule with no sugar alcohols listed.

why.claim: This cefdinir is a capsule.
The only inactive ingredient the label lists is carboxymethylcellulose calcium. No sorbitol or other sugar alcohol is listed.
Most medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel. Plain immediate-release medicines can often still be absorbed when that part remains.
Timed-release and coated designs are the ones usually avoided after bowel surgery. This capsule is not one of them.
How well a pill is absorbed depends mostly on how much healthy small bowel is left. Your length isn't known, so it's worth checking with your team.
Even in people without bowel surgery, the body absorbs only about a fifth of a cefdinir capsule dose.
Cefdinir also comes as a liquid. Liquids can be absorbed more reliably, but they often contain sugar alcohols that can cause more diarrhea.

why.claim: الدواء الذي وجدته هو قرص عادي.
معظم الأدوية تُمتص في الجزء العلوي من الأمعاء الدقيقة (أول الصائم)، لذلك كثير من الأقراص العادية يمكن أن تُمتص إذا بقي هذا الجزء.

الأدوية الممتدة أو المتأخرة المفعول (ومنها المغلفة معوياً) يُتجنب استخدامها عادة بعد استئصال كبير للأمعاء، لأنها تحتاج أمعاء طويلة لتُطلق الدواء. لذلك تأكد أن ما تأخذه هو القرص العادي.

في الدراسات، قلّ امتصاص 29 من 37 دواءً بعد استئصال جزء من الأمعاء، والأمر يختلف حسب الدواء، فلا يمكن التنبؤ بالنتيجة لشخص بعينه.
الأدوية الممتدة أو المتأخرة المفعول (ومنها المغلفة معوياً) يُتجنب استخدامها عادة بعد استئصال كبير للأمعاء، لأنها تحتاج مروراً طويلاً وطبيعياً في الأمعاء لتُطلق الدواء.

evidence.G:aga-sbs#anatomy-groups: Short bowel syndrome is described in three anatomy groups: end-jejunostomy (no colon), jejuno-colic (small bowel joined to part of the colon), and jejuno-ileo-colic (some ileum kept, joined to the colon). Advice on fluids and diet differs between these groups.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-release-forms: After extensive small-bowel resection, sustained-release and delayed-release (including enteric-coated) medicines are generally avoided because they depend on a long, normal transit to release the drug.
evidence.G:hong-2021#absorption-findings: Across studies reviewed, absorption was decreased for 29 of 37 drugs after intestinal resection, and 6 drugs lost clinical effect; the effect was drug-specific, so it cannot be turned into a single probability for one person.
evidence.G:pg139#liquid-forms: Liquid forms may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets in short bowel syndrome, but liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols that can increase output.
evidence.G:sood-2013#residual-length: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.

draft.ask: ASK: मेरी इलियोस्टॉमी है और 100 से 200 cm छोटी आँत है। क्या मेरे ORS में सोडियम शॉर्ट बाउल के लिए काफ़ी है, या मुझे ज़्यादा सोडियम वाला ORS लेना चाहिए?

careTeamAnswers.summary: इलियोस्टॉमी वाले एक दूसरे यूज़र ने बताया कि उनके अपने डॉक्टर ने कहा: WHO फ़ॉर्मूला दस्त के अचानक दौर के लिए बना था और उन्हें ज़्यादा नमक चाहिए।
एक दूसरे यूज़र ने बताया कि उनकी अपनी डाइटीशियन ने कहा: दुकान वाले कई ORS में शॉर्ट बाउल के मुकाबले सोडियम कम होता है, और उन्होंने अपनी मंज़ूर की हुई एक रेसिपी दी (यह डाइटीशियन द्वारा प्रमाणित है)।
एक दूसरे यूज़र ने बताया कि उनकी अपनी डाइटीशियन ने कहा: थोड़ा नींबू या बिना चीनी वाला फ़्लेवर आम तौर पर ठीक है, पर सॉर्बिटोल वाले फ़्लेवर से बचें।

swapToAskAbout.text: अगर आपका ORS पैकेट वाला WHO फ़ॉर्मूला या कोई आम दुकान वाला ड्रिंक है, तो अपनी टीम से पूछें कि क्या आपको शॉर्ट बाउल वाली सीमा (लगभग 90 से 120 mmol/L सोडियम) वाला ORS लेना चाहिए।

draft.verdict: जिन स्रोतों को मैंने देखा, उनमें आपके शरीर के लिए ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन (ORS) से कोई टकराव नहीं मिला। गाइडलाइन इसे शॉर्ट बाउल में पानी और नमक की कमी पूरी करने के लिए पसंदीदा पेय बताती हैं, बस यह जाँचना ज़रूरी है कि आपके ORS में नमक (सोडियम) कितना है।

why.claim: शॉर्ट बाउल सिंड्रोम में पानी और नमक की कमी पूरी करने के लिए ग्लूकोज़-नमक वाला ORS पसंदीदा पेय है।
ORS इसलिए काम करता है क्योंकि छोटी आँत में ग्लूकोज़ और नमक साथ-साथ सोखे जाते हैं और अपने साथ पानी भी अंदर ले जाते हैं। आपके पास 100 से 200 cm छोटी आँत है, और यही वह हिस्सा है जहाँ ORS असर करता है।
इलियोस्टॉमी वाले लोगों में पानी की कमी (डिहाइड्रेशन) और कम सोडियम का खतरा ज़्यादा होता है।
शॉर्ट बाउल के लिए आम तौर पर लगभग 90 से 120 mmol/L सोडियम वाला ORS सुझाया जाता है। यह बाज़ार में मिलने वाले कई रिहाइड्रेशन ड्रिंक्स से ज़्यादा है।
WHO का कम-ऑस्मोलैरिटी वाला ORS (सोडियम 75, क्लोराइड 65, ग्लूकोज़ 75, पोटैशियम 20, साइट्रेट 10 mmol/L) दस्त के अचानक दौर के लिए बनाया गया था। इसमें सोडियम शॉर्ट बाउल के लिए बताई गई सीमा से कम है।
आपकी जैसी बनावट (इलियोस्टॉमी) वाले लोगों के अनुभव मिले-जुले रहे: 14 में से 7 ने कहा कि मदद मिली, 6 ने कहा कि तकलीफ़ हुई।

G:aga-sbs#fluids-ors.text: A glucose-electrolyte oral rehydration solution (ORS) is the preferred drink to replace fluid and sodium losses in short bowel syndrome, especially with a jejunostomy.

G:pd-2017#ors-sodium.text: For short bowel syndrome, oral rehydration solutions with a sodium concentration of about 90 to 120 mmol/L are generally recommended; this is higher than many commercial rehydration drinks.

G:sood-2013#ileostomy-dehydration.text: People with an ileostomy are at higher risk of dehydration and low sodium, and medicines such as diuretics and laxatives can add to that risk.

G:who-ors#purpose.text: Oral rehydration solution works because glucose and sodium are absorbed together in the small bowel, carrying water with them.

G:who-ors#reduced-osmolarity-composition.text: WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS (2003) contains sodium 75 mmol/L, chloride 65, glucose 75, potassium 20 and citrate 10 mmol/L (total 245 mOsm/L). It was designed for acute diarrhea, and its sodium is below the range usually cited for short bowel syndrome.

G:aga-sbs#fluids-ors.text: A glucose-electrolyte oral rehydration solution (ORS) is the preferred drink to replace fluid and sodium losses in short bowel syndrome, especially with a jejunostomy.

G:pd-2017#hypotonic-colon.text: Most people with short bowel syndrome whose colon is in continuity tolerate ordinary hypotonic fluids such as water better than people with an end-jejunostomy, because the colon absorbs water and sodium.

G:pd-2017#ors-sodium.text: For short bowel syndrome, oral rehydration solutions with a sodium concentration of about 90 to 120 mmol/L are generally recommended; this is higher than many commercial rehydration drinks.

G:who-ors#purpose.text: Oral rehydration solution works because glucose and sodium are absorbed together in the small bowel, carrying water with them.

G:who-ors#reduced-osmolarity-composition.text: WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS (2003) contains sodium 75 mmol/L, chloride 65, glucose 75, potassium 20 and citrate 10 mmol/L (total 245 mOsm/L). It was designed for acute diarrhea, and its sodium is below the range usually cited for short bowel syndrome.

draft.verdict: పెడియాలైట్ లాంటి ఉప్పు-చక్కెర కలిసిన ORS పానీయం షార్ట్ బవెల్‌కు గైడ్‌లైన్లు ఎక్కువగా సూచించే రకమే, కానీ దుకాణాల్లో దొరికే చాలా ORSల్లో షార్ట్ బవెల్‌కు సూచించే దానికంటే ఉప్పు (సోడియం) తక్కువ ఉంటుంది, కాబట్టి ఇది మీకు సరిపోతుందో మీ డైటీషియన్‌ను అడగండి.

why.claim: షార్ట్ బవెల్‌లో పోయిన నీరు, ఉప్పును తిరిగి నింపడానికి గ్లూకోజ్-ఉప్పు కలిసిన ORS పానీయమే ఎక్కువగా ఇష్టపడే పానీయం.
చిన్న ప్రేగులో గ్లూకోజ్, సోడియం కలిసి శోషించబడతాయి, వాటితో పాటు నీటిని కూడా లోపలికి తీసుకెళ్తాయి. అందుకే ORS పని చేస్తుంది.
షార్ట్ బవెల్‌కు సాధారణంగా లీటరుకు సుమారు 90 నుండి 120 mmol సోడియం ఉన్న ORS సూచిస్తారు. ఇది దుకాణాల్లో దొరికే చాలా రీహైడ్రేషన్ పానీయాల కంటే ఎక్కువ.
WHO తక్కువ-ఆస్మోలారిటీ ORSలో సోడియం 75 mmol/L ఉంటుంది. దీన్ని అకస్మాత్తు విరేచనాల కోసం తయారు చేశారు, షార్ట్ బవెల్‌కు చెప్పే పరిధి కంటే ఇది తక్కువ.
మీ పెద్ద ప్రేగు (కోలన్) కలిసి ఉంది కాబట్టి, అది నీరు, ఉప్పును కొంత పీల్చుకుంటుంది. అందుకే జెజునోస్టమీ ఉన్నవాళ్లతో పోలిస్తే కోలన్ ఉన్నవాళ్లు మామూలు నీటిని ఎక్కువగా తట్టుకుంటారు.
సాధారణ స్పోర్ట్స్ డ్రింక్స్‌లో సోడియం తక్కువ, చక్కెర ఎక్కువ. అవి ORSకు బదులు కావు.
మీలాంటి శరీర నిర్మాణం (చిన్న ప్రేగు కోలన్‌కు కలిసి ఉన్నవారు) ఉన్న 12 మందిలో 8 మంది ORS తమకు సహాయపడిందని రాశారు, 2 మందికి ఇబ్బంది అయింది, 2 మందికి ఏ తేడా లేదు.

final.verdict: పెడియాలైట్ లాంటి ఉప్పు-చక్కెర కలిసిన ORS పానీయం షార్ట్ బవెల్‌కు గైడ్‌లైన్లు ఎక్కువగా సూచించే రకమే, కానీ దుకాణాల్లో దొరికే చాలా ORSల్లో షార్ట్ బవెల్‌కు సూచించే దానికంటే ఉప్పు (సోడియం) తక్కువ ఉంటుంది, కాబట్టి ఇది మీకు సరిపోతుందో మీ డైటీషియన్‌ను అడగండి.

why.claim: షార్ట్ బవెల్‌లో పోయిన నీరు, ఉప్పును తిరిగి నింపడానికి గ్లూకోజ్-ఉప్పు కలిసిన ORS పానీయమే ఎక్కువగా ఇష్టపడే పానీయం.
చిన్న ప్రేగులో గ్లూకోజ్, సోడియం కలిసి శోషించబడతాయి, వాటితో పాటు నీటిని కూడా లోపలికి తీసుకెళ్తాయి. అందుకే ORS పని చేస్తుంది.
షార్ట్ బవెల్‌కు సాధారణంగా లీటరుకు సుమారు 90 నుండి 120 mmol సోడియం ఉన్న ORS సూచిస్తారు. ఇది దుకాణాల్లో దొరికే చాలా రీహైడ్రేషన్ పానీయాల కంటే ఎక్కువ.
WHO తక్కువ-ఆస్మోలారిటీ ORSలో సోడియం 75 mmol/L ఉంటుంది. దీన్ని అకస్మాత్తు విరేచనాల కోసం తయారు చేశారు, షార్ట్ బవెల్‌కు చెప్పే పరిధి కంటే ఇది తక్కువ.
మీ పెద్ద ప్రేగు (కోలన్) కలిసి ఉంది కాబట్టి, అది నీరు, ఉప్పును కొంత పీల్చుకుంటుంది. అందుకే జెజునోస్టమీ ఉన్నవాళ్లతో పోలిస్తే కోలన్ ఉన్నవాళ్లు మామూలు నీటిని ఎక్కువగా తట్టుకుంటారు.
సాధారణ స్పోర్ట్స్ డ్రింక్స్‌లో సోడియం తక్కువ, చక్కెర ఎక్కువ. అవి ORSకు బదులు కావు.
మీలాంటి శరీర నిర్మాణం (చిన్న ప్రేగు కోలన్‌కు కలిసి ఉన్నవారు) ఉన్న 12 మందిలో 8 మంది ORS తమకు సహాయపడిందని రాశారు, 2 మందికి ఇబ్బంది అయింది, 2 మందికి ఏ తేడా లేదు.

evidence.G:pd-2017#hypotonic-colon: Most people with short bowel syndrome whose colon is in continuity tolerate ordinary hypotonic fluids such as water better than people with an end-jejunostomy, because the colon absorbs water and sodium.

draft.ask: ASK: Tengo intestino corto con el colon conectado. ¿Puedo tomar agua normal, o necesito una solución de rehidratación oral en algunos momentos?

careTeamAnswers.summary: Otra persona usuaria, también con el colon conectado, contó lo que le dijo su propia dietista: las personas con colon suelen tolerar mejor el agua, y su plan de líquidos se ajustó a su caso.

Otra persona usuaria, sin colon (yeyunostomía), contó lo que le dijo su propia dietista: sin colon, el agua sola puede sacar sal del cuerpo y aumentar las pérdidas. Esto no corresponde a su tipo de intestino.

diagram.label: A colon absorbs much of the water and salt

swapToAskAbout.text: Si pierde mucho líquido o tiene mucha diarrea, puede preguntar por una solución de rehidratación oral. Es la bebida preferida para reponer agua y sal en el intestino corto. Las guías citan un sodio de unos 90 a 120 mmol/L. Eso es más que la fórmula de la OMS, que tiene 75 mmol/L.

draft.verdict: Para su tipo de intestino, con el colon todavía conectado, no encontré nada que advierta contra el agua en las fuentes que revisé.

why.claim: La mayoría de las personas con intestino corto que conservan el colon conectado toleran mejor el agua que quienes tienen una yeyunostomía, porque el colon absorbe agua y sal.
La advertencia de limitar el agua sola es para personas con yeyunostomía terminal (sin colon). Ese no es su caso.
Las bebidas que sí conviene limitar, para cualquier tipo de intestino, son las muy azucaradas, como el jugo de fruta y los refrescos normales. Pueden aumentar la diarrea.
Las recomendaciones sobre líquidos cambian según el tipo de intestino, así que su plan de líquidos lo debe definir su equipo de salud.
Entre las personas con el intestino unido al colon que registraron el agua, 5 de 13 dijeron que les ayudó, 8 no notaron cambio y ninguna dijo que le hizo daño.

swapToAskAbout.text: Nếu bạn uống để bù nước, hãy hỏi về dung dịch bù nước (ORS) có đủ muối cho hội chứng ruột ngắn.

draft.verdict: Tôi không thấy gì trong các nguồn tôi đã kiểm tra nói rằng người có hậu môn nhân tạo hồi tràng như bạn phải tránh nước dừa. Nhưng không có tài liệu nào nói riêng về nước dừa, và nước dừa không phải là dung dịch bù nước (ORS).

why.claim: Người có hậu môn nhân tạo hồi tràng dễ bị mất nước và thiếu muối (natri) hơn người khác.
Dung dịch bù nước có đường và muối (ORS) là thức uống được ưu tiên để bù nước và muối bị mất trong hội chứng ruột ngắn.
Với hội chứng ruột ngắn, ORS thường được khuyên có natri khoảng 90 đến 120 mmol/L, cao hơn nhiều loại nước bù nước bán sẵn.
Nước ngọt nhiều đường như nước trái cây hay nước ngọt có ga có thể kéo nước vào ruột và làm tăng lượng ra ở túi, nên hạn chế. Nếu nước dừa bạn mua có thêm đường, hãy để ý điều này.
Khát, nước tiểu sẫm màu hoặc ít đi, chóng mặt khi đứng dậy, và lượng ra ở túi tăng là dấu hiệu mất nước. Hãy báo cho đội chăm sóc sớm.

draft.verdict: Pour Méthylin solution, je n'ai rien trouvé d'inquiétant dans les sources que j'ai consultées pour un intestin grêle relié au côlon, mais la liste complète des ingrédients sur la notice était coupée.

why.claim: Méthylin est un liquide (solution buvable), pas un comprimé à libération prolongée ou enrobé.
Les formes liquides peuvent être mieux absorbées que les comprimés en cas de syndrome de l'intestin court.

La plupart des médicaments sont absorbés dans le haut de l'intestin grêle. Un médicament simple, à libération immédiate, peut donc souvent être absorbé si cette partie est encore là. La longueur de votre intestin grêle n'est pas connue, c'est donc à vérifier.
Les médicaments liquides contiennent souvent des sucres-alcools (comme le sorbitol). Ceux-ci attirent l'eau dans l'intestin et peuvent augmenter la diarrhée.
La partie visible de la notice cite l'acide citrique et la glycérine comme ingrédients inactifs, mais la liste est coupée et la section complète des ingrédients inactifs manquait.
Prendre Méthylin avec un repas riche en graisses augmente un peu la quantité de médicament absorbée.

why.claim: Film coated ang tableta. Hindi ito nakalista bilang extended-release o delayed-release.

G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio.text: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.

G:aga-sbs#medications-release-forms.text: After extensive small-bowel resection, sustained-release and delayed-release (including enteric-coated) medicines are generally avoided because they depend on a long, normal transit to release the drug.

G:hong-2021#absorption-findings.text: Across studies reviewed, absorption was decreased for 29 of 37 drugs after intestinal resection, and 6 drugs lost clinical effect; the effect was drug-specific, so it cannot be turned into a single probability for one person.

G:hong-2021#drug-specific.text: Because the change in absorption differs from drug to drug, each medicine should be considered individually with the prescriber or pharmacist.

G:pd-2017#lactose.text: Lactose does not need to be removed for most people with short bowel syndrome; small portions of dairy, especially cheese and yogurt, are often tolerated.

G:pg139#malabsorption-suspect.text: If a medicine does not seem to produce its expected effect, malabsorption should be suspected and raised with the prescriber or pharmacist.

G:sood-2013#residual-length.text: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.

L:dosage_and_administration.text: Swallow the tablets whole.

L:pharmacokinetics.text: The absolute bioavailability of rosuvastatin is approximately 20%.

draft.verdict: L'étiquette ne dit pas à quel endroit de l'intestin l'oxcarbazépine s'absorbe, et comme ce comprimé est à libération prolongée, la façon dont il s'absorbera chez vous dépend surtout de la longueur d'intestin grêle qui vous reste : votre pharmacien peut vous aider à y voir clair.

why.claim: Sur l'\u00e9tiquette, ce m\u00e9dicament est un comprim\u00e9 \u00e0 lib\u00e9ration prolong\u00e9e. Il lib\u00e8re donc le m\u00e9dicament petit \u00e0 petit, pendant qu'il avance dans l'intestin.
L'\u00e9tiquette dit d'avaler ces comprim\u00e9s entiers, sans les couper, les \u00e9craser ni les m\u00e2cher.

Le seul renseignement de l'\u00e9tiquette sur l'absorption concerne les repas. Pris avec un repas tr\u00e8s gras, le comprim\u00e9 donne dans le sang la m\u00eame quantit\u00e9 de MHD (la substance mesur\u00e9e) qu'\u00e0 jeun. L'\u00e9tiquette ne dit pas dans quelle partie de l'intestin il s'absorbe.
De fa\u00e7on g\u00e9n\u00e9rale, la plupart des m\u00e9dicaments s'absorbent dans le haut de l'intestin gr\u00eale. Ce n'est pas une information propre \u00e0 l'oxcarbaz\u00e9pine.

Les formes \u00e0 lib\u00e9ration prolong\u00e9e ont besoin d'un long passage dans l'intestin. Si l'intestin est plus court ou si le transit est rapide, une partie de la dose peut sortir avant d'\u00eatre lib\u00e9r\u00e9e.
Apr\u00e8s une grande ablation de l'intestin gr\u00eale, on \u00e9vite en g\u00e9n\u00e9ral les formes \u00e0 lib\u00e9ration prolong\u00e9e.
L'absorption d\u00e9pend surtout de la longueur et de l'\u00e9tat de l'intestin gr\u00eale restant. Votre longueur n'est pas connue, donc on ne peut pas pr\u00e9voir votre cas.

Dans les \u00e9tudes, l'absorption a baiss\u00e9 pour 29 m\u00e9dicaments sur 37 apr\u00e8s une ablation de l'intestin. Mais l'effet change selon le m\u00e9dicament : on ne peut pas en tirer un chiffre pour une seule personne.
Les formes liquides s'absorbent parfois mieux, mais elles contiennent souvent des sucres-alcools qui peuvent augmenter les selles.

why.claim: Sur l'étiquette, ce médicament est un comprimé à libération prolongée.

De façon générale, la plupart des médicaments s'absorbent dans le haut de l'intestin grêle (le début du jéjunum). Ce n'est pas une information propre à l'oxcarbazépine.

Les formes à libération prolongée ont besoin d'un temps de passage suffisant dans l'intestin grêle. Si l'intestin est plus court ou si le transit est rapide, une partie de la dose peut sortir avant d'être libérée.
Après une grande ablation de l'intestin grêle, on évite en général les formes à libération prolongée.
L'absorption dépend surtout de la longueur et de l'état de l'intestin grêle restant. Votre longueur n'est pas connue, donc on ne peut pas prévoir votre cas.

Dans les études, l'absorption a baissé pour 29 médicaments sur 37 après une ablation de l'intestin. Mais l'effet change selon le médicament : on ne peut pas en tirer un chiffre pour une seule personne.
Les formes liquides s'absorbent parfois mieux, mais elles contiennent souvent des sucres-alcools qui peuvent augmenter les selles.

why.claim: Ang mga taong may stoma ay mas mataas ang panganib ng dehydration at mababang sodium, at puwedeng dagdagan ng mga diuretic ang panganib na iyon.
Ang mga palatandaan ng dehydration ay pagkauhaw, maitim o kaunting ihi, pagkahilo kapag tumatayo, at pagdami ng output sa stoma. Dapat itong sabihin agad sa inyong care team.
Ang likidong gamot ay puwedeng mas maayos ma-absorb kaysa sa tableta sa short bowel syndrome, pero madalas may sugar alcohol ang mga likidong gamot na nagpapataas ng output.
Ang gamot na ito ay suspension (likido), hindi extended-release.

Ang nakalistang inactive ingredients ay sorbic acid, potassium sorbate at citric acid. Pero kulang ang listahan, at wala ang buong seksyon ng inactive ingredients, kaya hindi ko makumpirma na walang sorbitol o ibang sugar alcohol.
Ang sorbitol at ibang sugar alcohol ay humihila ng tubig sa bituka at puwedeng magpataas ng output sa stoma.
Ayon sa label, mas tumataas ang dami ng gamot na na-absorb kapag ininom kasabay ng pagkaing mataas sa taba.

final.ask: ASK: May end-jejunostomy ako na walang colon. Gaano kalaki ang panganib ng dehydration o mababang sodium sa spironolactone, at may sorbitol ba o ibang sugar alcohol ang suspension na ito?

G:aga-sbs#dehydration-signs.text: Thirst, dark or reduced urine, dizziness on standing, and rising stoma output are warning signs of dehydration that should be raised with the care team promptly.

G:pg139#liquid-forms.text: Liquid forms may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets in short bowel syndrome, but liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols that can increase output.

G:pg139#sugar-alcohols.text: Sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol and other sugar alcohols are poorly absorbed, draw water into the gut, and can raise stoma output or diarrhea; they are common inactive ingredients in liquid medicines and sugar-free products.

G:sood-2013#ileostomy-dehydration.text: People with an ileostomy are at higher risk of dehydration and low sodium, and medicines such as diuretics and laxatives can add to that risk.

L:description.text: Inactive ingredients include sorbic acid, potassium sorbate, citric acid anhydrous,

L:pharmacokinetics.text: A high fat and high calorie meal (57% of the ~1000 kcal of the meal were from fat) increased the bioavailability of spironolactone (as measured by AUC) by approximately 90%.

why.claim: 대장이 이어져 있으면 물 같은 저장성 음료를 끝-공장루(jejunostomy)가 있는 사람보다 대체로 더 잘 견뎌요. 대장이 물과 소금을 흡수해 주기 때문이에요. 이 앱에 등록된 코코넛 워터 정보는 '저장성'이에요.
단당류가 진한 음료(가당 음료)는 장으로 물을 끌어당겨서, 단기장증후군에서는 보통 줄이라고 해요. 단맛을 더한 코코넛 워터라면 성분표를 확인해 보세요.
과일주스처럼 고장성이고 단 음료는 설사나 배출량을 늘릴 수 있어서, 몸 구조와 상관없이 줄이는 게 좋다고 해요.
잃은 수분과 소금을 채우는 데는 포도당-전해질 경구수액(ORS)을 가장 먼저 권해요. 코코넛 워터는 ORS가 아니에요.
단기장증후군에는 나트륨이 약 90~120 mmol/L인 ORS를 보통 권해요. 시중 음료 중에는 이보다 낮은 것이 많아요.

diagram.label: Most medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel

sourcesChecked: Guidelines: AGA SBS update, Hong 2021, Sood 2013, Practical Gastroenterology #139, Parrish & DiBaise 2017

आपका अपना लॉग: fenofibrate (कोई रिकॉर्ड नहीं)
draft.verdict: मैंने जो स्रोत देखे, उनमें Tricor गोली के लिए आपके शरीर से जुड़ी कोई खास चेतावनी नहीं मिली। लेकिन लेबल में यह नहीं लिखा कि यह दवा आंत के किस हिस्से में सोखी जाती है, इसलिए यह पक्का जवाब नहीं है।

why.claim: आपके सवाल का सीधा जवाब: लेबल यह नहीं बताता कि fenofibrate आंत के किस हिस्से में सोखी जाती है। लेबल बस इतना कहता है कि यह दवा पानी में लगभग नहीं घुलती।
आम तौर पर ज़्यादातर दवाएं छोटी आंत के ऊपरी हिस्से में सोखी जाती हैं। अगर वह हिस्सा बचा है, तो कई साधारण गोलियां अब भी सोखी जा सकती हैं।
लेबल में Tricor का रूप सिर्फ़ 'TABLET' लिखा है। इसमें धीरे-धीरे दवा छोड़ने वाली (extended-release) या कोटिंग वाली (delayed-release) गोली होने की बात नहीं लिखी।
जिन लोगों की आंत का बड़ा हिस्सा निकाला गया हो, उनके लिए धीरे-धीरे दवा छोड़ने वाली और कोटिंग वाली दवाओं से आम तौर पर बचा जाता है। Tricor के लेबल में ऐसी कोई बात नहीं लिखी।
यह भी जानना ज़रूरी है: एक review में आंत का हिस्सा निकाले जाने के बाद 37 में से 29 दवाएं कम सोखी गईं, और 6 दवाओं का असर ही चला गया। यह हर दवा के लिए अलग होता है, इसलिए पहले से कहना मुश्किल है।
दवा कितनी सोखी जाएगी, यह स्टोमा के प्रकार से ज़्यादा इस पर निर्भर करता है कि छोटी आंत कितनी लंबी और कितनी स्वस्थ बची है।

G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio.text: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.

G:aga-sbs#medications-release-forms.text: After extensive small-bowel resection, sustained-release and delayed-release (including enteric-coated) medicines are generally avoided because they depend on a long, normal transit to release the drug.

G:hong-2021#absorption-findings.text: Across studies reviewed, absorption was decreased for 29 of 37 drugs after intestinal resection, and 6 drugs lost clinical effect; the effect was drug-specific, so it cannot be turned into a single probability for one person.

G:sood-2013#residual-length.text: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.

L:description.text: Each tablet contains hypromellose 2910 (3 cps), docusate sodium, sucrose,

L:information_for_patients.text: to take TRICOR once daily, without regard to food, at the prescribed dose, swallowing each tablet whole.

L:pharmacokinetics.text: The absolute bioavailability of fenofibrate cannot be determined as the compound is virtually insoluble in aqueous media suitable for injection.

why.claim: आपके सवाल का सीधा जवाब: लेबल यह नहीं बताता कि fenofibrate आंत के किस हिस्से में सोखी जाती है। लेबल बस इतना कहता है कि यह दवा इंजेक्शन लायक पानी वाले घोल में लगभग नहीं घुलती।
आम तौर पर ज़्यादातर दवाएं छोटी आंत के ऊपरी हिस्से में सोखी जाती हैं। अगर वह हिस्सा बचा है, तो कई साधारण गोलियां अब भी सोखी जा सकती हैं।
लेबल में Tricor का रूप सिर्फ़ 'TABLET' लिखा है। इसमें धीरे-धीरे दवा छोड़ने वाली (extended-release) या कोटिंग वाली (delayed-release) गोली होने की बात नहीं लिखी।
जिन लोगों की आंत का बड़ा हिस्सा निकाला गया हो, उनके लिए धीरे-धीरे दवा छोड़ने वाली और कोटिंग वाली दवाओं से आम तौर पर बचा जाता है। Tricor के लेबल में ऐसी कोई बात नहीं लिखी।
यह भी जानना ज़रूरी है: एक review में आंत का हिस्सा निकाले जाने के बाद 37 में से 29 दवाएं कम सोखी गईं, और 6 दवाओं का असर ही चला गया। यह हर दवा के लिए अलग होता है, इसलिए पहले से कहना मुश्किल है।
दवा कितनी सोखी जाएगी, यह स्टोमा के प्रकार से ज़्यादा इस पर निर्भर करता है कि छोटी आंत कितनी लंबी और कितनी स्वस्थ बची है।
लेबल कहता है कि Tricor खाने के साथ या बिना खाने के ले सकते हैं, और हर गोली पूरी निगलनी है।
गोली में sucrose (एक तरह की चीनी) है। लेबल में बाकी सामग्री (inactive ingredients) की पूरी सूची नहीं थी।

evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-release-forms: After extensive small-bowel resection, sustained-release and delayed-release (including enteric-coated) medicines are generally avoided because they depend on a long, normal transit to release the drug.
evidence.G:hong-2021#absorption-findings: Across studies reviewed, absorption was decreased for 29 of 37 drugs after intestinal resection, and 6 drugs lost clinical effect; the effect was drug-specific, so it cannot be turned into a single probability for one person.
evidence.G:pd-2017#fat: Fat restriction is mainly useful when the colon is in continuity (because of oxalate and fatty-acid effects in the colon); with an end-jejunostomy, fat is an important energy source and is usually not restricted.
evidence.G:pg139#liquid-forms: Liquid forms may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets in short bowel syndrome, but liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols that can increase output.
evidence.G:pg139#time-release: Time-release formulations depend on adequate small-bowel transit time to release their drug; with a shortened bowel or rapid transit, part of the dose may leave the body before it is released.
evidence.G:sood-2013#colon-slow-release: The large intestine matters mainly for slow-release products, which may release part of their dose there; without a colon, those products have less time and surface to release.
evidence.G:sood-2013#ileostomy-dehydration: People with an ileostomy are at higher risk of dehydration and low sodium, and medicines such as diuretics and laxatives can add to that risk.
evidence.G:sood-2013#residual-length: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.

दवा कितनी सोखी जाएगी, यह स्टोमा के प्रकार से ज़्यादा इस बात पर निर्भर करता है कि बची हुई छोटी आंत कितनी लंबी और कितनी स्वस्थ है।
आंत का हिस्सा निकाले जाने के बाद, जाँची गई 37 में से 29 दवाएँ कम सोखी गईं। यह असर हर दवा में अलग होता है, इसलिए पहले से पक्का नहीं कहा जा सकता।
प्यास लगना, पेशाब गहरा या कम होना, खड़े होने पर चक्कर आना, या स्टोमा से निकलने वाले पानी का बढ़ना पानी की कमी के संकेत हैं। इन्हें जल्दी अपनी केयर टीम को बताएँ।

G:aga-sbs#dehydration-signs.text: Thirst, dark or reduced urine, dizziness on standing, and rising stoma output are warning signs of dehydration that should be raised with the care team promptly.

G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio.text: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.

G:hong-2021#absorption-findings.text: Across studies reviewed, absorption was decreased for 29 of 37 drugs after intestinal resection, and 6 drugs lost clinical effect; the effect was drug-specific, so it cannot be turned into a single probability for one person.

G:remane-2025#formulation-classes.text: Oral formulations can be grouped by dissolution risk in ostomy patients as noncritical (for example solutions and plain fast-dissolving tablets), potentially critical, and critical (for example extended-release and enteric-coated products).

why.claim: सादी, जल्दी घुलने वाली गोलियाँ स्टोमा वाले लोगों में कम जोखिम वाली मानी जाती हैं। धीरे-धीरे दवा छोड़ने वाली (extended-release) और कोटिंग वाली (enteric-coated) गोलियाँ ज़्यादा जोखिम वाली मानी जाती हैं।
ज़्यादातर दवाएँ छोटी आंत के ऊपरी हिस्से (जेजुनम की शुरुआत) में सोखी जाती हैं। इसलिए वह हिस्सा बचा हो, तो कई सादी गोलियाँ अब भी सोखी जा सकती हैं।
दवा कितनी सोखी जाएगी, यह स्टोमा के प्रकार से ज़्यादा इस बात पर निर्भर करता है कि बची हुई छोटी आंत कितनी लंबी और कितनी स्वस्थ है।
आंत का हिस्सा निकाले जाने के बाद, जाँची गई 37 में से 29 दवाएँ कम सोखी गईं। यह असर हर दवा में अलग होता है, इसलिए पहले से पक्का नहीं कहा जा सकता।
प्यास लगना, पेशाब गहरा या कम होना, खड़े होने पर चक्कर आना, या स्टोमा से निकलने वाले पानी का बढ़ना पानी की कमी के संकेत हैं। इन्हें जल्दी अपनी केयर टीम को बताएँ।

draft.verdict: Não encontrei nenhum problema nas fontes que verifiquei: o SINGULAIR é um comprimido revestido por película de liberação imediata, o tipo que costuma ser absorvido bem quando a parte de cima do intestino delgado está presente.

why.claim: A bula do SINGULAIR diz que ele \u00e9 um comprimido revestido por pel\u00edcula. N\u00e3o \u00e9 de libera\u00e7\u00e3o prolongada.

Comprimidos simples, que se dissolvem r\u00e1pido, est\u00e3o no grupo de menor risco de n\u00e3o se dissolver em pessoas com estomia. O maior risco \u00e9 com produtos de libera\u00e7\u00e3o prolongada ou com revestimento ent\u00e9rico.

A maioria dos rem\u00e9dios \u00e9 absorvida na parte de cima do intestino delgado. Por isso, muitos rem\u00e9dios simples de libera\u00e7\u00e3o imediata ainda s\u00e3o absorvidos quando essa parte continua no corpo.
A absor\u00e7\u00e3o dos rem\u00e9dios depende mais do comprimento e da sa\u00fade do intestino delgado que resta do que do tipo de estomia. Voc\u00ea tem mais de 200 cm de intestino delgado.
N\u00e3o ter o intestino grosso importa mais para rem\u00e9dios de libera\u00e7\u00e3o lenta. Isso n\u00e3o se aplica ao SINGULAIR, que \u00e9 de libera\u00e7\u00e3o imediata.
Em m\u00e9dia, 64% do rem\u00e9dio tomado pela boca chega ao sangue. Esse n\u00famero vem de estudos com pessoas em geral, n\u00e3o com pessoas com estomia.
A vers\u00e3o gen\u00e9rica de montelucaste tem lactose entre os ingredientes inativos. As diretrizes que consultei n\u00e3o falam sobre lactose em comprimidos.

final.verdict: Não encontrei nenhum problema nas fontes que verifiquei. A bula diz que o SINGULAIR é um comprimido revestido por película. why.claim: A bula do SINGULAIR diz que ele é um comprimido revestido por película.

Comprimidos simples, que se dissolvem rápido, estão no grupo de menor risco de não se dissolver em pessoas com estomia. O maior risco é com produtos de liberação prolongada ou com revestimento entérico.
A maioria dos remédios é absorvida na parte de cima do intestino delgado. Por isso, muitos remédios simples de liberação imediata ainda podem ser absorvidos quando essa parte continua no corpo.
A absorção dos remédios depende mais do comprimento e da saúde do intestino delgado que resta do que do tipo de estomia.
Não ter o intestino grosso importa principalmente para remédios de liberação lenta.
Em média, 64% do remédio tomado pela boca chega ao sangue.

why.claim: 含葡萄糖和盐的口服补液盐，是短肠综合征补水、补钠的首选饮品。
它起作用，是因为葡萄糖和钠在小肠里一起被吸收，同时把水带进身体。
短肠综合征通常推荐钠含量约 90–120 mmol/L 的补液盐，比很多市售补液饮品更高。
世卫组织低渗配方的钠是 75 mmol/L，原本是为急性腹泻设计的，低于短肠常用的范围。
小肠接着结肠的人，结肠能吸收不少水和盐，所以一般比空肠造口的人更能耐受普通饮水。
普通运动饮料钠低、糖高，不能代替短肠用的补液盐。

G:aga-sbs#fluids-ors.text: A glucose-electrolyte oral rehydration solution (ORS) is the preferred drink to replace fluid and sodium losses in short bowel syndrome, especially with a jejunostomy.

G:pd-2017#hypotonic-colon.text: Most people with short bowel syndrome whose colon is in continuity tolerate ordinary hypotonic fluids such as water better than people with an end-jejunostomy, because the colon absorbs water and sodium.

G:who-ors#purpose.text: Oral rehydration solution works because glucose and sodium are absorbed together in the small bowel, carrying water with them.

G:who-ors#reduced-osmolarity-composition.text: WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS (2003) contains sodium 75 mmol/L, chloride 65, glucose 75, potassium 20 and citrate 10 mmol/L (total 245 mOsm/L). It was designed for acute diarrhea, and its sodium is below the range usually cited for short bowel syndrome.

why.claim: 含葡萄糖和盐的口服补液盐，是短肠综合征补水、补钠的首选饮品。
它起作用，是因为葡萄糖和钠在小肠里一起被吸收，同时把水带进身体。
短肠综合征通常推荐钠含量约 90–120 mmol/L 的补液盐，比很多市售补液饮品更高。
世卫组织低渗配方的钠是 75 mmol/L，原本是为急性腹泻设计的，低于短肠常用的范围。
小肠接着结肠的人，结肠能吸收不少水和盐，所以一般比空肠造口的人更能耐受普通饮水。
普通运动饮料钠低、糖高，不能代替短肠用的补液盐。
和您解剖结构相同（小肠接结肠）的用户里，12 人中有 8 人记录有帮助，2 人没变化，2 人觉得更差。

evidence.G:aga-sbs#fluids-ors: A glucose-electrolyte oral rehydration solution (ORS) is the preferred drink to replace fluid and sodium losses in short bowel syndrome, especially with a jejunostomy.
evidence.G:pd-2017#hypotonic-colon: Most people with short bowel syndrome whose colon is in continuity tolerate ordinary hypotonic fluids such as water better than people with an end-jejunostomy, because the colon absorbs water and sodium.
evidence.G:pd-2017#ors-sodium: For short bowel syndrome, oral rehydration solutions with a sodium concentration of about 90 to 120 mmol/L are generally recommended; this is higher than many commercial rehydration drinks.
evidence.G:pd-2017#sports-drinks: Typical sports drinks are low in sodium and high in sugar compared with an SBS oral rehydration solution, so they are not a substitute for it.
evidence.G:who-ors#purpose: Oral rehydration solution works because glucose and sodium are absorbed together in the small bowel, carrying water with them.
evidence.G:who-ors#reduced-osmolarity-composition: WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS (2003) contains sodium 75 mmol/L, chloride 65, glucose 75, potassium 20 and citrate 10 mmol/L (total 245 mOsm/L). It was designed for acute diarrhea, and its sodium is below the range usually cited for short bowel syndrome.
evidence.T:000000000011820care_team_answers: My dietitian said many store-bought ORS products are lower in sodium than what is used for short bowel, and gave me a recipe she approved.
evidence.T:000000000011821care_team_answers: Mine said a little lemon or sugar-free flavoring is usually fine but to avoid sorbitol-based flavorings.
evidence.T:000000000011822care_team_answers: My doctor said the WHO formula was designed for acute diarrhea and mine needs more salt.

draft.ask: ASK: Tengo yeyunostomía terminal con menos de 100 cm de intestino. ¿Cómo comprobamos con análisis si absorbo bien este fenofibrato, y hay otra forma que se absorba mejor?

diagram.label: Most medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel

sourcesChecked: Guidelines: immediate-release absorption in short bowel / jejunostomy
Guidelines: poorly soluble drugs and malabsorption
draft.verdict: No se sabe con certeza si se absorbe bien: es una tableta normal, no de liberación prolongada, y eso ayuda. Pero usted tiene menos de 100 cm de intestino y la etiqueta dice que el fenofibrato casi no se disuelve en agua, así que vale la pena revisarlo con su equipo.

why.claim: La etiqueta dice que es una tableta. No dice que sea de liberación prolongada ni con capa entérica.
Las tabletas normales que se disuelven rápido están en el grupo de menor riesgo para personas con ostomía. Las de liberación prolongada o con capa entérica son las de más riesgo.
La mayoría de los medicamentos se absorben en la primera parte del intestino delgado. Por eso muchas pastillas normales se pueden absorber si esa parte sigue ahí.
Lo bien que se absorbe un medicamento depende sobre todo de cuánto intestino delgado queda y de qué tan sano está. Usted tiene menos de 100 cm, y eso puede reducir la absorción.
Después de quitar parte del intestino, la absorción bajó en 29 de 37 medicamentos estudiados. Cambia según el medicamento, así que no se puede predecir para una persona.
Por eso las guías dicen que cada medicamento se debe revisar por separado con el médico o el farmacéutico.
La etiqueta dice que el fenofibrato casi no se disuelve en agua.

Algo nuevo que conviene saber: si un medicamento no parece hacer su efecto, puede ser que no se esté absorbiendo. Las guías dicen que hay que comentarlo con quien lo recetó o con el farmacéutico. Con el fenofibrato, eso se puede ver en sus análisis de sangre.
La etiqueta dice que se puede tomar con o sin comida y que hay que tragar cada tableta entera. Pregunte antes de cambiar la forma de tomarla.
Las formas líquidas a veces se absorben mejor que las tabletas en el intestino corto, pero muchas llevan azúcares tipo alcohol (como el sorbitol) que pueden aumentar lo que sale por el estoma.
La tableta lleva sacarosa (azúcar). La lista completa de ingredientes inactivos no estaba en la etiqueta, así que no se puede descartar el sorbitol.
Nadie con su misma anatomía ni con otra ha anotado todavía cómo le fue con el fenofibrato.

diagram.label: Most medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel

G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio.text: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.

G:hong-2021#absorption-findings.text: Across studies reviewed, absorption was decreased for 29 of 37 drugs after intestinal resection, and 6 drugs lost clinical effect; the effect was drug-specific, so it cannot be turned into a single probability for one person.

G:hong-2021#drug-specific.text: Because the change in absorption differs from drug to drug, each medicine should be considered individually with the prescriber or pharmacist.

G:pg139#liquid-forms.text: Liquid forms may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets in short bowel syndrome, but liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols that can increase output.

G:pg139#malabsorption-suspect.text: If a medicine does not seem to produce its expected effect, malabsorption should be suspected and raised with the prescriber or pharmacist.

G:remane-2025#formulation-classes.text: Oral formulations can be grouped by dissolution risk in ostomy patients as noncritical (for example solutions and plain fast-dissolving tablets), potentially critical, and critical (for example extended-release and enteric-coated products).

why.claim: La etiqueta dice que es una tableta. No dice si es de liberación prolongada ni si tiene capa entérica.
Las tabletas normales que se disuelven rápido están en el grupo de menor riesgo para personas con ostomía. Las de liberación prolongada o con capa entérica son las de más riesgo.
La mayoría de los medicamentos se absorben en la primera parte del intestino delgado. Por eso muchas pastillas normales se pueden absorber si esa parte sigue ahí.
Lo bien que se absorbe un medicamento depende más de cuánto intestino delgado queda y de qué tan sano está que del tipo de estoma.
Después de quitar parte del intestino, la absorción bajó en 29 de 37 medicamentos estudiados. Cambia según el medicamento, así que no se puede predecir para una persona.
Por eso cada medicamento se debe revisar por separado con quien lo recetó o con el farmacéutico.
La etiqueta dice que el fenofibrato casi no se disuelve en agua.
Si un medicamento no parece hacer su efecto, puede ser que no se esté absorbiendo. Las guías dicen que hay que comentarlo con quien lo recetó o con el farmacéutico.
La etiqueta dice que se puede tomar con o sin comida y que hay que tragar cada tableta entera. Pregunte antes de cambiar la forma de tomarla.
Las formas líquidas a veces se absorben mejor que las tabletas en el intestino corto, pero muchas llevan azúcares tipo alcohol que pueden aumentar lo que sale por el estoma.
La tableta lleva sacarosa (azúcar). La lista completa de ingredientes inactivos no estaba disponible, así que no se sabe qué más contiene.

draft.verdict: Para o AG-X comprimido, não encontrei nada nas fontes que verifiquei que impeça seu uso com uma ileostomia e mais de 200 cm de intestino delgado. Mas o rótulo tem pouca informação, então vale confirmar com o farmacêutico.

why.claim: O AG-X é um comprimido comum (não é de liberação prolongada).
Comprimidos comuns, que se dissolvem rápido, estão no grupo de menor risco de não dissolver em quem tem estomia. Os de maior risco são os de liberação prolongada e os com revestimento entérico.
A maioria dos remédios é absorvida no começo do intestino delgado. Por isso, muitos comprimidos comuns ainda são absorvidos quando essa parte continua lá.
A absorção depende mais do tamanho e da saúde do intestino delgado que sobrou do que do tipo de estomia. Você tem mais de 200 cm.
Os ingredientes listados no rótulo são magnésio, vitamina D e pó de ginseng vermelho. Nenhum deles é sorbitol nem outro açúcar-álcool, que podem aumentar o débito da bolsa.
Quem tem ileostomia corre mais risco de desidratação e de sódio baixo. Remédios como laxantes podem aumentar esse risco. Então, observe se o débito da bolsa muda.

Atenção: faltam várias partes do rótulo, como a descrição, a farmacocinética e a forma de apresentação. Por isso, não consegui confirmar qual é o ingrediente ativo nem a dose. Minha confiança é baixa.

swapToAskAbout.text: Demandez \u00e0 votre \u00e9quipe si une solution de r\u00e9hydratation orale vous conviendrait pour une partie de ce que vous buvez. Pour le syndrome du gr\u00eale court, les sources citent en g\u00e9n\u00e9ral une teneur en sodium d'environ 90 \u00e0 120 mmol/L. C'est plus que la SRO de l'OMS (75 mmol/L).

draft.verdict: Je n'ai rien trouvé contre l'eau gazeuse nature dans les sources que j'ai consultées. Mais aucune source ne parle de l'eau gazeuse elle-même, et ce qu'on y ajoute (sucre, édulcorants, caféine) change la réponse.

why.claim: Avec une il\u00e9ostomie, le risque de d\u00e9shydratation et de manque de sel est plus \u00e9lev\u00e9. Il est donc important de bien choisir ce que vous buvez.

Les boissons sucr\u00e9es, comme le soda classique ou le jus de fruits, attirent l'eau dans l'intestin. Elles peuvent faire monter le d\u00e9bit de la stomie. Choisissez une eau gazeuse sans sucre ajout\u00e9.

Les eaux \u00ab sans sucre \u00bb aromatis\u00e9es peuvent contenir du sorbitol, du xylitol ou d'autres polyols. Ces sucres-alcools peuvent aussi faire monter le d\u00e9bit. Lisez bien les ingr\u00e9dients.
La caf\u00e9ine peut augmenter les pertes de liquide. M\u00e9fiez-vous des boissons gazeuses qui en contiennent.

On conseille en g\u00e9n\u00e9ral de boire par petites gorg\u00e9es tout au long de la journ\u00e9e plut\u00f4t que beaucoup d'un coup. Beaucoup d'\u00e9quipes conseillent aussi de boire en dehors des repas.
Pour remplacer l'eau et le sel perdus, la boisson recommand\u00e9e est une solution de r\u00e9hydratation orale (SRO) avec du glucose et du sel. L'eau gazeuse ne la remplace pas.

La soif, des urines fonc\u00e9es ou plus rares, des vertiges en vous levant, ou un d\u00e9bit de stomie qui augmente sont des signes de d\u00e9shydratation. Parlez-en vite \u00e0 votre \u00e9quipe soignante.

G:pd-2017#caffeine-alcohol.text: Caffeine and alcohol can increase output and fluid losses and are usually limited in short bowel syndrome.

G:pd-2017#ors-sodium.text: For short bowel syndrome, oral rehydration solutions with a sodium concentration of about 90 to 120 mmol/L are generally recommended; this is higher than many commercial rehydration drinks.

G:pg139#sugar-alcohols.text: Sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol and other sugar alcohols are poorly absorbed, draw water into the gut, and can raise stoma output or diarrhea; they are common inactive ingredients in liquid medicines and sugar-free products.

G:sood-2013#ileostomy-dehydration.text: People with an ileostomy are at higher risk of dehydration and low sodium, and medicines such as diuretics and laxatives can add to that risk.

swapToAskAbout.text: You could ask the care team whether a different form of the same medicine might suit your parent better. The guidelines say that when a medicine may be poorly absorbed, liquid, dissolvable, topical, or non-oral forms of the same drug may be considered.

final.verdict: Being a liquid may help this nitrofurantoin get absorbed in your parent's body, but it contains sorbitol, which can make diarrhea worse, so it's worth checking with the pharmacist.

why.claim: This medicine is a liquid (an oral suspension), not a tablet.
With short bowel, liquids may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets. But liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols that can increase output.
The label lists sorbitol as one of the ingredients in this liquid.
Sorbitol is poorly absorbed. It pulls water into the gut and can make diarrhea or stoma output worse.
How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.
The label says food, or agents that delay stomach emptying, can increase how much nitrofurantoin the body takes in.

evidence.G:aga-sbs#antimotility: Antimotility medicines (for example loperamide) are a mainstay to slow transit and reduce output; timing relative to meals is set by the care team.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#fluids-hypertonic: Hypertonic, sugary drinks such as fruit juice and regular soda pull water into the gut and can raise stoma output or diarrhea in short bowel syndrome; they are best limited regardless of anatomy.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-alternatives: When a medicine may be poorly absorbed after resection, the care team may consider liquid, dissolvable, topical, or non-oral forms of the same drug instead.
evidence.G:pd-2017#hypotonic-colon: Most people with short bowel syndrome whose colon is in continuity tolerate ordinary hypotonic fluids such as water better than people with an end-jejunostomy, because the colon absorbs water and sodium.
evidence.G:pg139#extended-release-avoid: Extended-release products are generally avoided after extensive resection; an immediate-release or liquid version of the same drug is often a question worth asking the pharmacist about.
evidence.G:pg139#liquid-forms: Liquid forms may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets in short bowel syndrome, but liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols that can increase output.
evidence.G:pg139#sugar-alcohols: Sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol and other sugar alcohols are poorly absorbed, draw water into the gut, and can raise stoma output or diarrhea; they are common inactive ingredients in liquid medicines and sugar-free products.
evidence.G:sood-2013#residual-length: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.

draft.verdict: لم أجد شيئاً في المصادر التي راجعتها يدل على مشكلة واضحة في قرص نيورونتين العادي مع جسمك، لكن هناك أمران مهمان: كمية الدواء التي يمتصها الجسم تقلّ كلما كبرت الجرعة اليومية، ونشرة نيورونتين التي وجدتها تتكلم عن الكبسولات لا عن القرص المغلّف الذي كتبته.

why.claim: كيف يمتصه الجسم: أغلب الأدوية تُمتص في الجزء العلوي من الأمعاء الدقيقة. لذلك يمكن امتصاص كثير من الأدوية العادية سريعة المفعول ما دام هذا الجزء موجوداً.

حسب النشرة، نسبة الدواء التي يمتصها الجسم تقلّ كلما زادت الجرعة اليومية. تكون حوالي ٦٠٪ مع ٩٠٠ ملغ في اليوم، وتنزل إلى حوالي ٢٧٪ مع ٤٨٠٠ ملغ في اليوم. يعني ذلك أن مضاعفة الجرعة لا تضاعف الكمية التي تصل إلى الجسم.
هذا دواء سريع المفعول، وليس ممتد المفعول. أصحاب الفغرة تُعتبر عندهم الأقراص العادية سريعة الذوبان غير حرجة من ناحية الذوبان. أما الأقراص ممتدة المفعول أو المغلفة معوياً فتُعتبر حرجة.

بعد استئصال جزء كبير من الأمعاء الدقيقة، يتجنب الأطباء عادةً الأدوية ممتدة المفعول أو المغلفة معوياً، لأنها تحتاج أمعاء طويلة لتطلق الدواء. لذلك إن اقترح عليك أحد نوعاً ممتد المفعول من الجابابنتين، اسأل عنه أولاً.
نشرة نيورونتين التي وجدتها مكتوبة للكبسولات. تقول إن الكبسولات تُبلع كاملة مع الماء. هذه النشرة لا تخص القرص المغلّف الذي كتبته، فتأكد من الصيدلي ما هو الشكل الذي معك بالضبط.
نشرة أقراص الجابابنتين تذكر في بيانات المنتج الجابابنتين ونشا الذرة والكوبوفيدون، ولا يظهر بينها سوربيتول. لكن قسم المكونات غير الفعالة كان غير موجود، فقد تكون القائمة ناقصة.
مدى امتصاص الأدوية يرتبط بطول الأمعاء الدقيقة المتبقية وصحتها أكثر من نوع الفغرة.
في الدراسات، قلّ امتصاص ٢٩ دواءً من ٣٧ بعد استئصال جزء من الأمعاء. هذا يختلف من دواء لآخر، ولا يمكن توقعه بدقة لشخص بعينه.
لأن الامتصاص بعد الاستئصال صعب التوقع، قد يراقب الفريق الطبي مفعول الدواء عن قرب.

G:aga-sbs#medications-alternatives.text: When a medicine may be poorly absorbed after resection, the care team may consider liquid, dissolvable, topical, or non-oral forms of the same drug instead.

G:aga-sbs#medications-monitoring.text: For drugs with a narrow therapeutic range, clinicians may check drug blood levels or watch the clinical effect closely, because absorption after resection is hard to predict.

G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio.text: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.

G:aga-sbs#medications-release-forms.text: After extensive small-bowel resection, sustained-release and delayed-release (including enteric-coated) medicines are generally avoided because they depend on a long, normal transit to release the drug.

G:hong-2021#absorption-findings.text: Across studies reviewed, absorption was decreased for 29 of 37 drugs after intestinal resection, and 6 drugs lost clinical effect; the effect was drug-specific, so it cannot be turned into a single probability for one person.

G:remane-2025#formulation-classes.text: Oral formulations can be grouped by dissolution risk in ostomy patients as noncritical (for example solutions and plain fast-dissolving tablets), potentially critical, and critical (for example extended-release and enteric-coated products).

G:sood-2013#residual-length.text: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.

L:dosage_and_administration.text: NEURONTIN capsules should be swallowed whole with water.

L:pharmacokinetics.text: Bioavailability of gabapentin is approximately 60%, 47%, 34%, 33%, and 27% following 900, 1200, 2400, 3600, and 4800 mg/day given in 3 divided doses, respectively.

swapToAskAbout.text: Bupropion also comes in an immediate-release form. Plain tablets that dissolve fast are in the lower-risk group for people with an ostomy. Ask the prescriber or pharmacist whether that form would suit your parent.

draft.verdict: Forfivo XL is an extended-release tablet, and without a working colon your parent's gut may give it less time to release all of its medicine, so this is worth checking with the pharmacist.

why.claim: Forfivo XL is a film-coated, extended-release tablet.
The label says it should be swallowed whole, not crushed, divided, or chewed.
Time-release pills need enough time moving through the small bowel to let out their medicine. If the gut is shorter or moves fast, some of the dose can leave the body before it is released.
Slow-release products may let out part of their dose in the colon. Your parent's colon is not connected, so the pill has less time and less surface to release.
Extended-release products are in the highest-risk group for not dissolving properly in people with an ostomy.
How well pills are absorbed depends mostly on how long and healthy the remaining small bowel is. Your parent has over 200 cm, which may help, but only the care team can judge this.
Taking it with food raised the total amount of bupropion in the body by 25%.

evidence.G:aga-sbs#antimotility: Antimotility medicines (for example loperamide) are a mainstay to slow transit and reduce output; timing relative to meals is set by the care team.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#dehydration-signs: Thirst, dark or reduced urine, dizziness on standing, and rising stoma output are warning signs of dehydration that should be raised with the care team promptly.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#diet-simple-sugars: Concentrated simple sugars (sweets, syrups, sweetened drinks) draw water into the bowel and are generally limited in short bowel syndrome.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#fluids-ors: A glucose-electrolyte oral rehydration solution (ORS) is the preferred drink to replace fluid and sodium losses in short bowel syndrome, especially with a jejunostomy.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.
evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-release-forms: After extensive small-bowel resection, sustained-release and delayed-release (including enteric-coated) medicines are generally avoided because they depend on a long, normal transit to release the drug.
evidence.G:pd-2017#hypotonic-colon: Most people with short bowel syndrome whose colon is in continuity tolerate ordinary hypotonic fluids such as water better than people with an end-jejunostomy, because the colon absorbs water and sodium.
evidence.G:pd-2017#lactose: Lactose does not need to be removed for most people with short bowel syndrome; small portions of dairy, especially cheese and yogurt, are often tolerated.
evidence.G:pd-2017#ors-sodium: For short bowel syndrome, oral rehydration solutions with a sodium concentration of about 90 to 120 mmol/L are generally recommended; this is higher than many commercial rehydration drinks.
evidence.G:pg139#enteric-coating: Enteric-coated and delayed-release products are designed to pass the stomach before dissolving; with rapid transit, the coating may not dissolve in time, and some pass through intact.
evidence.G:pg139#liquid-forms: Liquid forms may be absorbed more reliably than solid tablets in short bowel syndrome, but liquid medicines often contain sugar alcohols that can increase output.
evidence.G:pg139#sugar-alcohols: Sorbitol, xylitol, mannitol and other sugar alcohols are poorly absorbed, draw water into the gut, and can raise stoma output or diarrhea; they are common inactive ingredients in liquid medicines and sugar-free products.
evidence.G:pg139#time-release: Time-release formulations depend on adequate small-bowel transit time to release their drug; with a shortened bowel or rapid transit, part of the dose may leave the body before it is released.
evidence.G:sood-2013#residual-length: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.
evidence.G:who-ors#purpose: Oral rehydration solution works because glucose and sodium are absorbed together in the small bowel, carrying water with them.
evidence.G:who-ors#reduced-osmolarity-composition: WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS (2003) contains sodium 75 mmol/L, chloride 65, glucose 75, potassium 20 and citrate 10 mmol/L (total 245 mOsm/L). why.claim: This gabapentin is a liquid (a solution), not an extended-release or coated pill.

Most medicines are taken in by the upper small bowel, so many plain medicines can still be absorbed when that part remains.

The label lists xylitol among the inactive ingredients.

draft.verdict: Tramadol ER is a slow-release tablet, and guidelines say these often don't release all their medicine in a shortened gut like your parent's, so it's worth checking with the pharmacist.

why.claim: This tablet is an extended-release (slow-release) form.
The label says to swallow it whole with liquid.
After a large part of the small bowel is removed, slow-release and coated medicines are usually avoided. They need a long, normal trip through the gut to release the drug.
When the bowel is shorter or moves things through fast, part of the dose may leave the body before it is released.
Slow-release products may release part of their dose in the colon. Your parent's colon is not connected, so the tablet has less time and less gut to release in.
The label's absorption numbers come from healthy people, not from people with a shortened bowel.

draft.verdict: I can't tell you crushing Naprelan is fine. It's a slow-release tablet, and the guidelines say to check with a pharmacist before you crush any medicine.

why.claim: The guidelines say to ask a pharmacist before you change how you take a medicine, and that includes crushing it, splitting it or switching products.
Naprelan is a film-coated, extended-release tablet. That means it is made to release the medicine slowly.
The label says the tablet breaks up in your stomach into tiny slow-release particles. These travel through the small intestine and into the first part of the large intestine.
The label lists a polymer, ammoniomethacrylate copolymer Type A, among the tablet's ingredients.
Slow-release products can release part of their dose in the large intestine. Your colon isn't connected, so these products have less time and less surface to release.
Time-release medicines need enough time in the small bowel. If things move through fast, part of the dose may leave your body before it is released.
The Naprelan label I could check doesn't have a 'do not crush' line. Its warnings, patient leaflet and instructions sections were missing, so I can't tell you what it says about crushing.

why.claim: The label says to swallow MS Contin whole. It says not to cut, break, chew, crush or dissolve it, because that risks a possibly fatal dose.

final.verdict: I can't tell you crushing is OK: the label says to swallow this extended-release tablet whole and not crush it, and nothing I found says crushing helps it absorb better, so please call your pharmacist before your next dose.

why.claim: This is an extended-release tablet.
The label says to swallow it whole and not crush, split, or chew it.
One guideline says people with a stoma should talk to a pharmacist before crushing, splitting, or switching a medicine.
With a colostomy, most of the small bowel is usually still there, and pills are often absorbed normally. That isn't a guarantee.
Most medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel.
Extended-release pills are in the 'critical' group for not dissolving fully in people with an ostomy.
The label I found is for Aplenzin, another brand of extended-release bupropion, not Wellbutrin XL itself. The label's warnings section was missing, so I couldn't check what it says.

evidence.G:aga-sbs#medications-proximal-absorptio: Most oral medicines are absorbed in the upper small bowel (the first part of the jejunum), so many plain immediate-release drugs can still be absorbed when that segment remains.
evidence.G:pd-2017#hypotonic-colon: Most people with short bowel syndrome whose colon is in continuity tolerate ordinary hypotonic fluids such as water better than people with an end-jejunostomy, because the colon absorbs water and sodium.
evidence.G:pd-2017#thickening-foods: Starchy, low-fiber foods such as white rice, bananas, potatoes, pasta and plain crackers are often reported to thicken output.
evidence.G:remane-2025#formulation-classes: Oral formulations can be grouped by dissolution risk in ostomy patients as noncritical (for example solutions and plain fast-dissolving tablets), potentially critical, and critical (for example extended-release and enteric-coated products).
evidence.G:remane-2025#patient-education: In the pilot study, 11 of 50 interviewed ostomy patients had seen undissolved medicine, and over 60% said they had not been told how an ostomy can affect their medicines.
evidence.G:remane-2025#tablet-in-pouch: An intact tablet or shell seen in the pouch can mean the medicine did not dissolve, or it can be an empty shell left after the drug was released. It is worth showing the pharmacist; it is not proof either way.
evidence.G:sood-2013#ask-before-changing-form: Patients should consult a pharmacist before changing the dose form of a medicine, such as crushing, splitting or switching products.
evidence.G:sood-2013#colostomy: With a colostomy, most of the small bowel is usually intact and oral medicines are often absorbed normally; but the stoma type alone does not tell you remaining small-bowel length, so it is not a guarantee.
evidence.G:sood-2013#residual-length: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.
evidence.L:description: Each tablet contains the labeled amount of bupropion hydrobromide and the inactive ingredients: ethylcellulose
evidence.L:dosage_and_administration: APLENZIN should be swallowed whole and not crushed, divided, or chewed.
evidence.L:pharmacokinetics: The presence of food did not affect the peak concentration and time to peak plasma concentration of bupropion; the area under the curve was increased by 19%.

Talk to a pharmacist before changing how you take a medicine, such as crushing, splitting or switching products.
Your worry makes sense. In a shorter or faster gut, part of a timed-release dose may leave the body before it's released.

G:aga-sbs#medications-alternatives.text: When a medicine may be poorly absorbed after resection, the care team may consider liquid, dissolvable, topical, or non-oral forms of the same drug instead.

G:aga-sbs#medications-release-forms.text: After extensive small-bowel resection, sustained-release and delayed-release (including enteric-coated) medicines are generally avoided because they depend on a long, normal transit to release the drug.

G:pg139#crushing-immediate-release.text: For plain immediate-release tablets only, crushing or dissolving may improve absorption in some patients; this is a decision for the pharmacist. Crushing extended-release or enteric-coated products defeats their design and can be dangerous.

G:pg139#enteric-coating.text: Enteric-coated and delayed-release products are designed to pass the stomach before dissolving; with rapid transit, the coating may not dissolve in time, and some pass through intact.

G:pg139#extended-release-avoid.text: Extended-release products are generally avoided after extensive resection; an immediate-release or liquid version of the same drug is often a question worth asking the pharmacist about.

G:pg139#time-release.text: Time-release formulations depend on adequate small-bowel transit time to release their drug; with a shortened bowel or rapid transit, part of the dose may leave the body before it is released.

G:sood-2013#ask-before-changing-form.text: Patients should consult a pharmacist before changing the dose form of a medicine, such as crushing, splitting or switching products.

G:sood-2013#residual-length.text: How well oral medicines are absorbed tracks the length and health of the remaining small bowel more than the type of stoma.

L:pharmacokinetics.text: Diltiazem is well absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract and is subject to an extensive first-pass effect, giving an absolute bioavailability (compared to intravenous administration) of about 40%.

draft.verdict: لا تسحق هذا القرص ولا تقسمه بنفسك: النشرة تقول إنه لا يُقسم ولا يُمضغ ولا يُسحق، والإرشادات تقول إن سحق الأقراص ممتدة المفعول يُفسد طريقة عملها وقد يكون خطيرًا. الأفضل أن تسأل الصيدلي عن نسخة عادية أو سائلة.

why.claim: النشرة تقول بوضوح إن أقراص الميترونيدازول ممتدة المفعول لا تُقسم ولا تُمضغ ولا تُسحق.
هذا قرص مغلّف ممتد المفعول، أي أنه مصمَّم ليطلق الدواء ببطء.
الإرشادات تقول إن سحق الأقراص ممتدة المفعول أو المغلفة معويًا يُفسد تصميمها وقد يكون خطيرًا. سحق الأقراص العادية فقط قد يساعد بعض المرضى، وهذا قرار يعود للصيدلي.
يجب استشارة الصيدلي قبل تغيير شكل الدواء، مثل السحق أو التقسيم أو تبديل المنتج.
النشرة تقول إن الأكل وحده يغيّر طريقة إطلاق هذا القرص للدواء، فهو حساس لأي تغيير.
مع ذلك، قلقك في محلّه: الأدوية ممتدة المفعول تحتاج وقتًا كافيًا في الأمعاء، ومع أمعاء قصيرة قد يخرج جزء من الجرعة قبل أن يُطلق.
بدون قولون، يكون لهذه الأقراص البطيئة وقت ومساحة أقل لإطلاق الدواء.
الإرشادات تقترح سؤال الصيدلي عن نسخة عادية (سريعة الإطلاق) أو سائلة من نفس الدواء بدلًا من النسخة ممتدة المفعول.
معظم الأدوية تُمتص في الجزء العلوي من الأمعاء الدقيقة، لذلك كثير من الأدوية العادية يمكن أن تُمتص إذا بقي هذا الجزء.

الإرشادات تقول إن سحق الأقراص ممتدة المفعول أو المغلفة معويًا يُفسد تصميمها وقد يكون خطيرًا. سحق الأقراص العادية فقط قد يساعد بعض المرضى، وهذا قرار يعود للصيدلي.
يجب استشارة الصيدلي قبل تغيير شكل الدواء، مثل السحق أو التقسيم أو تبديل المنتج.
النشرة تقول إن تناول هذا القرص مع الطعام، مقارنةً بالصيام، يزيد سرعة امتصاصه ويغيّر خصائص الإطلاق الممتد.
مع ذلك، قلقك في محلّه: الأدوية ممتدة المفعول تحتاج وقتًا كافيًا في الأمعاء، ومع أمعاء قصيرة قد يخرج جزء من الجرعة قبل أن يُطلق.
بدون قولون، يكون لهذه الأقراص البطيئة وقت ومساحة أقل لإطلاق الدواء.
الإرشادات تقترح سؤال الصيدلي عن نسخة عادية (سريعة الإطلاق) أو سائلة من نفس الدواء بدلًا من النسخة ممتدة المفعول.
معظم الأدوية تُمتص في الجزء العلوي من الأمعاء الدقيقة، لذلك كثير من الأدوية العادية يمكن أن تُمتص إذا بقي هذا الجزء.

why.claim: The label says ELEPSIA XR should be taken whole. Do not split or cut the tablets.
It is an extended-release tablet. That means it is made to let the medicine out slowly over time.
Guidelines say to talk to a pharmacist before changing how you take a medicine, including crushing, splitting, or switching products.
Your worry makes sense. Slow-release products can let out part of their dose in the large bowel, and without a colon they have less time and space to do that.

draft.verdict: The label text I have doesn't say whether Coreg CR can be opened and mixed into yogurt, and it does say the contents must not be crushed or chewed, so please ask your pharmacist before you try this.

why.claim: Coreg CR is an extended-release capsule.
The label says Coreg CR and its contents should not be crushed, chewed, or taken in divided doses. The part of the label I could see says nothing either way about opening the capsule onto food.
Short bowel guidance says crushing extended-release products defeats how they are designed to work and can be dangerous. Whether opening the capsule changes anything is a question for the pharmacist.

After a large part of the small bowel is removed, slow-release medicines are generally avoided.
If a medicine may not absorb well after bowel surgery, the care team may look at other forms of the same drug instead.
